commands.name: install
commands.description: Install dependencies and reconcile the lockfile with package.json. NOT `npm ci`, and the difference is load-bearing: bootstrap prepares a tree that is being changed, so a turn that adds a dependency must be able to record it. `npm ci` refuses a lockfile that does not match, which made taking any dependency at all impossible through the belt. CI keeps `npm ci` — see .github/workflows/verify.yml — so the lockfile is still authoritative wherever the verdict counts (ADR 011). The lockfile diff is the sensor here; it does not block, and a change that grows it must be accounted for in the reason given.

commands.name: format
commands.description: Apply the repository's own formatting. Declared as bootstrap and ordered after install, because it runs prettier from node_modules and a tree that has not installed cannot format. It writes to the tree — that is the point, and it is why it is not a gate.

commands.name: build
commands.description: Emit dist/ from src/ using tsconfig.build.json. Bootstrap rather than gate for the same reason format is: it writes to the tree, and a gate whose verdict describes a tree it changed is not a verdict. Ordered after install because tsc comes from node_modules.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: The bar: typecheck, test, lint. One script, so the gate the belt runs and the gate CI runs cannot drift apart (S1). A `pretest` hook runs `npm run build` first, automatically, via npm's own pre-script convention — added because two of the tests here spawn the real compiled dist/cli/review.js, and dist/ is gitignored; CI runs `npm ci` && `npm run verify` and never a separate build step, so a fresh checkout had no binary for those tests to reach, while every local run had one already, left over from prepare_repository's own bootstrap chain (install, format, build, then gates). This does not reopen ADR 017 (`build` and `format` are bootstrap steps, not gates, because a gate whose verdict describes a tree it changed is not a verdict): `format` rewrites the tracked source the gate itself then judges, so a gate that formats is judging its own edit; `build` produces dist/, which is gitignored, disposable, and never the thing `verify` is a verdict about — typecheck, test and lint still run against the source exactly as committed. Building first makes the artifact current before it is spawned; it does not change what is being judged.

commands.name: cli
commands.description: Start the emitted binary and check it refuses an empty diff. The only check in this repository that runs the artifact rather than the source, and the only one that can catch the emitted files landing somewhere bin does not point. Costs nothing: an empty diff returns before any client is constructed.

commands.name: staleness-guard
commands.description: Spawn the cli gate's own script against two constructed trees — one with no dist/ at all, one with a dist/ that holds a file but no dist/cli/review.js — and check it refuses the first, naming staleness specifically, and does not refuse the second for that reason. Exists because the freshness guard inside check-cli.mjs was itself unverified: the pure function beneath it (buildFreshness.mjs) is covered thoroughly by unit tests and the guard's own wiring was not, which is the same defect one level up that the guard exists to catch one level down. Neither fixture depends on a modification time.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Run the review panel against the HEAD commit. A release step rather than a gate because it costs money — one model call per lens — and a gate that bills on every verification is a gate someone turns off. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment; without it the run reports which setting is missing and where to put it, and exits red without calling anything.

commands.name: review-branch
commands.description: Run the review panel against a diff between two refs — by default the current branch's own work against main (`git diff main...HEAD`), the same subject CI's check reviews — unlike `review`, which reviews only the HEAD commit. Both ends are nameable: AIGENCY_REVIEW_BRANCH_BASE (default `main`) and AIGENCY_REVIEW_BRANCH_HEAD (default `HEAD`). Both are also positional arguments (`node review-branch.mjs [base] [head]`), and positional wins over environment wins over default — the only channel a step declared here can carry, since a declared command's argv is fixed at write time and nothing available to run it can set its environment. A diff between two refs needs no checkout, so this can review a branch other than the one currently checked out — a ref that does not exist is refused by name, before anything is spawned or measured, and both refs are named if both are wrong. A release step for the same reason `review` is: it costs money, one model call per lens, and a gate that bills on every verification is a gate someone turns off. Refuses rather than reviews when the diff exceeds AIGENCY_REVIEW_BRANCH_MAX_CHARS (default 200000 characters), naming the measured size, the cap, and the gap — that refusal is not a judgement about the change. An empty diff against the base exits 0: nothing is wrong, there is nothing to review. Writes its report to .review-report/branch__<base>__<head>.md and the matching .json, so two different pairs reviewed from the same tree cannot collide. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the same way review does.

commands.name: review-main-vs-s24a-lens-set
commands.description: Review s24a/lens-set's own work against main — the specific pair review-branch.mjs's positional arguments exist to carry, named explicitly here because a declared command's argv is the only channel a step run through this belt can use to say which two refs it means. THIS DOES NOT GENERALISE — it is not a pattern to copy for the next branch under review. A step declared per subject means a fresh declaration for every pull request reviewed this way, which does not scale past this one review; the general-purpose route stays AIGENCY_REVIEW_BRANCH_BASE/_HEAD or a positional argument supplied by whoever invokes review-branch.mjs directly. This entry exists only because, for a step declared in aigency.json, that is the one way to name a subject at all. The third positional argument, 400000, raises the cap for this review only: s24a/lens-set is three stories on one branch (S24a, S15, S25), not one, and its diff — 303,719 characters — refuses correctly against the ordinary 200,000-character cap, because the cap is naming a real pull-request-size problem, not a wrong number. The raise is a deliberate one-off, made in argv — the one channel a declared step fully controls; a declared env block cannot do this, since it can only forward a variable already set in the process that started the belt, by name, and never set a value — to read findings that have been unreadable since before last night, not a judgement that 200,000 is wrong, and not a change to the script's own default.
